sections.content:
3,185 people

were counted on the census as "pre-press technicians" in England and Wales in March 2021.

This makes this type of work the third least common occupation reported on the census.

Pre-press technicians prepare, format and compose text and graphics in a form suitable for use in a variety of print processes.

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "pre-press technicians" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 50 to 54 years. Of the whole working population 11.7% were aged 50 to 54 years. For people working as "pre-press technicians", 13% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "pre-press technicians" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "pre-press technicians" included:

  • butchers
  • welding trades
  • metal working machine operatives

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "pre-press technicians" there were more men than women (72.2% compared with 27.8%).

This means "pre-press technicians" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "textiles, printing and other skilled trades".

Men made up 72.2% and women made up 27.8% of "pre-press technicians"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "pre-press technicians" included:

  • managers in logistics
  • musicians
  • managers and proprietors in agriculture and horticulture

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "pre-press technicians" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged under 30 years old, we see there is a higher proportion of women with this occupation than men.

The percentage of men and women who are "pre-press technicians" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "pre-press technicians", 8.7% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (76.2% compared with 23.8%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (82.8%) than self-employed (17.2%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was London. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Leeds, this is in the region of the Yorkshire & Humberside.
